entries.content:
The core arithmetic is consistent, but Claude can be undercounted.

- Codex subtracts cached tokens from input and reasoning tokens from output because its provider fields overlap. It then sums all model requests, including sub-agents. See [agent_provider_protocol.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_provider_protocol.js:20) and [agent_streaming_adapter.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_streaming_adapter.js:562).
- Claude’s input, cache-creation, and cache-read counters are already separate, so adding them is correct. [Anthropic confirms this formula](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits).
- The defect is that [agent_claude_events.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_claude_events.js:152) treats missing Claude cache counters as zero. Existing tests explicitly allow result events containing only input and output. Because cached tokens commonly dominate Claude Code usage, this can produce a severely low total.
- Claude reasoning remains inside output tokens. This differs from Codex’s breakdown but does not affect the total.

Proposed solution: create one shared Claude turn-usage accumulator for both streaming and one-shot execution. Record each unique assistant message’s usage by message ID, including sub-agent messages. Use the complete terminal result when all four counters exist; otherwise use the deduplicated assistant-message total. Add regression tests for missing terminal cache counters, repeated assistant messages, and sub-agent usage.
